cov_px.description:
The covariance of each image point, px², one per point; absent or
empty when not stated. Within one calibration input either every
view states them or none does.

points_2d.description: The matching image points `[u, v]`, pixels.

points_3d.description: 3D points `[x, y, z]` in the target frame, metres.

Iso3Schema.description:
JSON Schema proxy for [`Iso3`] (`nalgebra::Isometry3<f64>`).

`nalgebra` does not implement [`schemars::JsonSchema`], so `*Export` and
parameter types that embed [`Iso3`] annotate the field with
`#[cfg_attr(feature = "schemars", schemars(with = "Iso3Schema"))]`
(or `Vec<Iso3Schema>` / `Option<Iso3Schema>`). This proxy mirrors the exact
serde wire format of `Isometry3`:
`{ "rotation": [qx, qy, qz, qw], "translation": [tx, ty, tz] }`.

It exists only to describe that shape to `schemars`; it is never
constructed at runtime.

rotation.description: Unit quaternion `[qx, qy, qz, qw]` (i, j, k, w order).

PointCovariance.description:
The covariance of one observed image point, px²: the symmetric matrix
`[[xx, xy], [xy, yy]]`.

It states the point's measurement noise. A calibration whose views carry
covariances weighs each reprojection residual by its inverse (it
*whitens* it): an uncertain point counts less, and an elongated one is
trusted more across its long axis than along it. A uniform weight `w` on
every point corresponds to the covariance `I / w`.

Constructed only through [`PointCovariance::new`] (or deserialization),
which checks that it is finite and positive definite.

# Example

```
use vision_calibration_core::PointCovariance;

// σ = 0.3 px along u, 0.1 px along v, uncorrelated.
let cov = PointCovariance::new(0.09, 0.0, 0.01).unwrap();
assert_eq!(cov.yy(), 0.01);
assert!(PointCovariance::new(1.0, 2.0, 1.0).is_err()); // not positive definite
```

xx.description: Variance along the image `u` axis, px².

yy.description: Variance along the image `v` axis, px².

obs.description:
Target corners + laser pixels per camera (same shape as
[`RigLaserlineView`]).

RigLaserlineView.description:
Per-view observations for a rig-level laserline calibration.

Both `cameras` and `laser_pixels` are indexed by `cam_idx ∈ [0, num_cameras)`.
A slot is `None` when that camera had no usable data in this view (occlusion,
out-of-FOV, etc.).  An empty inner `Vec` is accepted but treated the same as
`None` by the solver.

cameras.description:
Target correspondences per camera (`cam_idx` → `Option<CorrespondenceView>`).

`None` means the camera did not see the calibration target in this view.
The slice length must equal `RigLaserlineDataset::num_cameras`.

laser_pixels.description:
Laser pixel observations per camera (`cam_idx` → `Option<Vec<Pt2>>`).

`None` means the camera has no usable laser data for this view.
The slice length must equal `RigLaserlineDataset::num_cameras`.
